subject: Post-demo: Acme reranker POC — infra checklist (SDK, auth, structured output, retries)
messages:
From: Alex Silva <alex@acme-logistics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-team@acme-logistics.com
Date: 2027-05-17T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from demo — questions on SDK, structured output, and error behavior

Thanks for the demo earlier — the reranker examples were helpful. A few quick follow-ups from the engineering team so we can scope the POC: 

1) SDK and auth: do you have a language-agnostic SDK guide and recommended auth flows for server-to-server (we prefer mTLS but can use API keys + KMS). Need examples for token rotation and short-lived credentials.

2) Structured output / tool-calling: for our reranker we need deterministic JSON output (score, explanation tokens, and optional tool call to a scoring microservice). How do you recommend encoding structured responses and validating them on the client side?

3) Rate limits & quotas: our expected baseline is 8 QPS for rerank jobs and spikes up to 120 QPS during batch windows. What’s the typical per-tenant soft quota and how does Redwood signal imminent throttling?

4) 429s & retries: we need a safe retry/backoff strategy (idempotency concerns since many requests update our local counters). Is there a recommended request-id or idempotency token pattern?

If you can send a short technical checklist and any runbook snippets we can review with infra tomorrow, that'd be great.

– Alex
Senior Platform Engineer
Acme Logistics

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Silva <alex@acme-logistics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-17T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up from demo — questions on SDK, structured output, and error behavior

Alex — thanks for the great questions and for flagging the QPS targets. Below is a concise technical checklist and next steps; attaching a short SDK quickstart and our integration runbook.

Summary / ask: we propose a 2-week POC with a small canary traffic stream (8–12 QPS steady, scaled to bursts to 120 QPS) to validate throughput and reranker quality. Please confirm access to a staging VPC and whether you prefer us to use mTLS or API keys for the POC.

Checklist (high level):
- SDK + auth
  - Languages: we have SDKs for Python/Go/Node; fallback is our HTTP API. Attached: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf.
  - Auth options: API key + short-lived tokens via your KMS (recommended for quick POC) OR mTLS for stricter network auth. We can provide rotation scripts for both.
  - Sample header: X-Redwood-Request-Id: UUID, X-Redwood-Idempotency-Token: sha256(request-body) (optional on POSTs that mutate your DB).

- Structured output / tool-calling
  - Use JSON schema validation client-side. We recommend the model return a top-level JSON object with fields {"items": [...], "meta": {"scores": [...], "explanations": [...]}}.
  - For tool calls, use the function-calling surface (we return a deterministic call payload) + verify signature header on the microservice.

- Rate limits / quotas
  - Per-tenant soft quota: default 100 RPS for hosted tenants; soft quota throttles with 429 + Retry-After header. You can request a temporary uplift for the POC.
  - Signals: 429, 503-surge, and a small X-Redwood-Queue-Time header (ms) indicate short queues.

- Retries + idempotency
  - Client pattern: short-circuit retries for idempotent GETs; for POSTs that mutate downstream, require an idempotency token.
  - Request-ID: include X-Redwood-Request-Id (UUIDv4) on every request. This is logged and surfaces in trace links.
  - Backoff: use exponential backoff with full jitter (base=200ms, max=10s, 6 retries). On 429s respect Retry-After if present.

Action items / timeline:
- You: confirm auth approach (mTLS vs API key) and grant staging VPC peering by EOD Tue.
- Us: share an Integration Runbook (attached) and a short script to add X-Redwood-Request-Id into your client interceptor.
- Meeting: propose a 30-min infra sync on 2027-05-18 10:00 PT to walk the runbook.

Attachments:
- redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (SDK install + auth snippets)
- integration-runbook.md (POC steps, canary settings, metrics to capture)
- acme-poc-mvp-requirements.xlsx (your list converted to POC checklist)

If helpful, Marissa will follow up with more details on retry windows and idempotency tokens.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Silva <alex@acme-logistics.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-team@acme-logistics.com
Date: 2027-05-18T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up from demo — questions on SDK, structured output, and error behavior

Thanks Neha — team reviewed. A couple clarifications before the infra sync: 

- We prefer mTLS but need a short checklist for the cert lifecycle in the POC. Can you provide a cert-rotation cadence and any automation you recommend?
- For per-tenant soft quota: you mentioned 100 RPS default — can you confirm what happens when we exceed it? For our batch window we will reach 120 QPS for ~10 minutes; want to avoid cascading failures.
- On idempotency tokens: we store scoring state in our service; if Redwood retries a request, we need to know whether to re-apply scoring or dedupe. Is the idempotency token guaranteed to be stable across retries from Redwood callers, or do we need to generate it client-side?

We'll join the sync — thanks, Alex

> Quick note: we also need the sample JSON schema for the reranker output so we can wire our validator.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Silva <alex@acme-logistics.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Follow-up from demo — questions on SDK, structured output, and error behavior

Alex — quick technical clarifications from the product/ops side to make the POC safe at scale. TL;DR: mTLS + client-side idempotency token is the cleanest path; we recommend a short 429-safety window and explicit replay/dedupe protocol.

mTLS certs
- Rotation: recommended 90-day rotation with automated renewal via ACME for POC; for air-gapped environments we provide a rotation script in integration-runbook.md.
- Automation: we typically hand over a small Ansible role that pulls certs and reloads your sidecar (we can run it in your staging project).

Quota behavior (what happens when you exceed soft quota)
- Soft quota exceeded: requests receive 429 with Retry-After and X-Redwood-Quota-Bucket header (current-usage/limit). Short bursts within the configured burst window are allowed; sustained overage goes to hard throttle and returns 429s without Retry-After.
- Recommended POC setting: configure a per-tenant burst allowance of +40% for 15 minutes (covers your 120 QPS spike). We'll create a temporary uplift for the POC and monitor queue-time.

Idempotency / request-id pattern
- Request-id (X-Redwood-Request-Id) is generated by caller and must be stable across client retries. Redwood logs that id and surfaces it in our tracing; we do not rewrite it.
- Idempotency token: for mutating calls, include X-Redwood-Idempotency-Token (sha256 of canonicalized request payload + client-salt). If present, Redwood will dedupe duplicate POST processing for up to 24 hours. If absent, treat POSTs as non-idempotent and do not retry blindly.

Retry/backoff recommendation
- For GET-like or idempotent requests: exponential backoff with full jitter; sample: sleep = random_between(0, base*2^attempt), base=150ms, max=8s, attempts=6.
- For POSTs with idempotency token: allow up to 3 retries with longer base (base=300ms) and require checking for a 409/duplicate response header instead of blindly reapplying state.

Example header snippets to include in your client interceptor:
- X-Redwood-Request-Id: 2f9f9a2b-3d2f-4f33-9b5b-1c6a2b4f7e9c
- X-Redwood-Idempotency-Token: f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d1e0f

I'll bring the JSON schema for reranker output to the infra sync (it's a one-page schema). See the attached runbook. Looking forward to the call — we'll have ops monitoring and can flip the temporary quota uplift during the test window.

— Marissa
Group Product Manager, Redwood Inference
